newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bellwether Cetes rate up on inflation worry.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bellwether Cetes rate up on inflation worry.

text.p: Mexico's key one-month Cetes rate increased at Banco de Mexico's primary auction on Tuesday, rising on expectations of higher inflation in December, analysts said.
The rate on the one-month treasury bill rose eight basis points to 27.37 percent, Banco de Mexico said. This was the second week in a row that the bellwether rate rose at the auction.
The rise this week was well below expectations -- a survey of 11 Cetes dealers by Reuter earlier in the day found expectations of an average increase of 94 basis points to 28.23 percent.
Some analyst were forecasting a rise of up to 121 basis points on the one-month paper.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, meeting earlier on Tuesday, decided to leave rates unchanged, which helped ease pressure on rates in Mexico, analysts said.
Demand was also strong, rising to 11.87 billion pesos from 11.39 billion pesos the week before.
"Traders remained bullish on Mexico despite some forecasts of higher than originally expected first two weeks of December CPI," MMS International said in a commentary.
Still the rate on the one-month paper increased. Last week the one-month paper rate broke a three-week decline to rise slightly at the auction as well.
Inflation is seen spiking to as high as three percent or more in December on the back of a series of wage and price hikes earlier this month.
The main factor is a strong hike in transportation tariffs, economists have said.
Inflation is also seen being a factor in January, and that was also reflected in the hike in rates on the three-month paper. that rose 28 basis points to 26.85 percent in the auction.
The Reuters survey had found expectations of a rise of 54 basis points to 27.11 percent.

The six-month paper rates, however, fell at the auction, showing that market players expect inflation to ease after January. The six month paper rate showed a decline of 14 basis points to 25.62 percent.
Demand, however, continued weak on the one-year paper as market concerns over key mid-term elections next year in Mexico remained.
Demand was only 1.651 billion pesos on the 600 million pesos worth of one-year paper on offer, for a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.75.
The rate on the one-year paper reflected this, as the 350-day paper was assigned at 25.68 percent compared to 25.59 percent on 358-day paper last week.
